# HELIOS / MonadoBlade

> Governed, C#-first Windows control and AI orchestration platform.

Canonical repository: M0nado/helios-platform
Integration contract: /config/integrations/event-contract.schema.json
Repository ownership: /config/integrations/repositories.json
Agent communication: /docs/architecture/UNIFIED_AGENT_COMMUNICATION.md
Capability backlog: /config/capabilities/major-capabilities.v1.json

## Engine routing

C# is the secure front-facing backbone and orchestrator. It keeps GUI, identity, vault, safety flags, online/Fabric/hybrid coordination, typed APIs, reliability, and clean object-shaped service boundaries simple. C++ is the high-speed partner for security-sensitive native helpers, performance, reactive profiles, memory, CPU, GPU, rendering, internet/download optimization, and algorithms that need low overhead. F# is the deep learning, analytics, scoring, prediction, optimization, and mathematical decision engine shared by everyone. Python is used deliberately for AIHub, LLM agents, Linux/WSL2, LangChain-style ecosystems, geometry/ML libraries, and provider glue, then hands results back through C# so all engines can use them.

### C#: front-facing secure orchestration backbone

Use C# for the main GUI, WinUI3 shell, secure API boundaries, vault integration, permissions, live automation flags, online and hybrid control, GitHub/Azure/Fabric coordination, object-shaped service contracts, reliability, configuration, state management, and every place where complexity needs to be hidden behind simple typed interfaces. C# should decide where work goes, keep the system understandable, prevent redundant paths, and make every engine easy to use. It should call F# for learning, C++ for hot paths, and Python for AIHub/provider/Linux libraries while keeping data contracts clean and safe.

Skills: WinUI3 GUI, typed service contracts, vault access, policy gates, hybrid orchestration, GitHub/Azure command routing, object models, dependency injection, safe APIs, settings UX, security boundaries, cross-engine dispatch.
Route when optimizing: security, reliability, maintainability, operator clarity, API shape, vault safety, hybrid readiness, testability.

### C++: native performance/security/rendering/hot-path engine

Use C++ whenever HELIOS needs low-cost, high-performance work that benefits from native memory control, predictable CPU usage, SIMD/vectorization, fast graph comparison, rendering overlays, GPU-adjacent pipelines, checksums, download or network throughput helpers, profiling, secure memory wiping, partition/device validation, and reactive desktop profile calculations. C++ should not replace the C# framework; it should act as a powerful engine called by C# through clean boundaries. It is ideal for hot algorithms, desktop rendering performance, memory-sensitive security helpers, large commit/repository graph scoring, and any repeated operation where Python or managed code would waste CPU or memory.

Skills: SIMD/vectorization, memory control, rendering overlays, GPU-adjacent batching, secure buffers, checksums, network throughput, download optimization, large graph comparison, profile kernels, partition validation, native scoring.
Route when optimizing: latency, CPU cost, memory pressure, GPU/render load, security sensitivity, repeat count, data size, interop safety.

### F#: deep learning analytics prediction scoring engine

Use F# as the shared intelligence engine for deep learning style scoring, analytics, predictions, ranking, search, async queries, mathematical modeling, anomaly detection, optimization, natural-selection style prompt and tool scoring, branch/commit issue priority, security/performance tradeoff analysis, cost-quality-speed balancing, module/submodule fit, and fleet XP progression. F# should be present throughout AIHub because it turns raw outcomes into decisions everyone can reuse. C# calls it through stable contracts, C++ supplies fast numeric or graph inputs when needed, and Python supplies specialized AI library outputs. F# makes all engines smarter together.

Skills: prediction, ranking, statistical scoring, async queries, optimization, anomaly detection, agent XP analytics, cost-quality-speed fusion, module fit, branch priority, security analytics, performance analytics.
Route when optimizing: prediction confidence, learning value, math clarity, score explainability, parallelism, signal quality, reuse, decision impact.

### Python: AIHub LLM agent Linux and special-library bridge

Use Python when the best capability comes from AIHub provider libraries, LLM agent frameworks, local model tooling, Linux/WSL2 automation, LangChain-style ecosystems, geometry or machine learning libraries, report generation, quick automation, and provider adapters for OpenAI, Claude, Ollama, Codex, Copilot, or other tools. Python should not become the core orchestrator when C#, F#, or C++ are better. It should gather external intelligence, run specialized libraries, and pass structured results back to C# so F# can score them and C++ can accelerate repeated hot work. Python remains valuable but intentionally focused.

Skills: OpenAI adapters, Claude adapters, Ollama/local models, LangChain-style tools, Linux automation, WSL2, special ML libraries, geometry libraries, report generation, provider glue, agent prompts, API probes.
Route when optimizing: library advantage, provider coverage, Linux need, agent/LLM fit, speed to automate, handoff quality, dependency risk, replaceability.

## AI provider boundaries

OpenAI API and Codex integrations belong behind AIHub provider adapters; use structured outputs, bounded tool permissions, correlation IDs, evaluation evidence, and secret references rather than embedded keys. Claude API and Claude Code use the same provider-neutral command/result envelope and cannot bypass approval gates. Hermes routes bounded work, XCore evaluates it, and Guardian blocks secrets, privileged Windows changes, tenant mutations, and production deployment without review.

## Safe setup and operations

Azure automation uses workload identity federation, managed identity, Key Vault, least privilege, Bicep validation, and what-if before apply. Windows disk, BitLocker, WDAC/AppLocker, firewall, Entra/RBAC, Intune, Purview, secret rotation, and production actions remain dry-run and approval gated. Never place credentials, raw fleet evidence, model weights, logs, caches, VHDX files, or local databases in Git.

## Development checks

Run `python3 scripts/knowledge/generate_llms_txt.py --check` to detect discovery-document drift, `python3 scripts/knowledge/validate_capabilities.py` to validate the consolidated 50-capability dependency graph, and `python3 scripts/knowledge/plan_capability_issues.py` to preview reviewable issue packets. Packet generation is local-only and never creates issues, branches, cloud resources, or privileged machine changes.
